title: Nine Stems of String
subtitle: 一束与一串 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 一束与一串（生活与学习·居家与器物）
meta: 主题语境：一束与一串（生活与学习·居家与器物）　|　核心词汇：bunch　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bunch 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my mother was sent to tie ① a bunch she could not carry, and she said the carrying was the whole of the lesson. The ② bunch, meaning the flowers and not the string, was nine stems wide and was taken by whoever came last; a bunch, she said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ bunch in that hall had the same ribbon, and the ④ bunch at the front, meaning the one the girl held and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever tied properly. A bunch, my grandmother said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the water is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bunch was the whole of the morning, meaning the gathering it stood for and not the flowers. The ⑥ bunch, meaning the gathering and not any of that, is the only thing in a village that everybody brings and nobody questions; a bunch, he said, is either something you tie or the only word that means both flowers and a gathering. She said the gathering is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ bunch had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the ribbon. The ⑧ bunch of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine stems and eleven years of tying; a bunch, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ bunch I remember is the one at the front, which was given in 1976 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ bunch, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being given; every bunch, she said, is a gathering that has agreed to look like flowers. She said the gathering was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 束（指那些花本身，与绳子相对）
C. 固定搭配：tie a bunch 扎一束（花）
D. n. 束（指厅里每一束）
E. n. 束（指前面那一束）
F. n. 束（抽象：它所代表的聚会）
G. n. 那场聚会（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bunch she could not carry
The bunch, meaning the flowers and not the string
bunch was the whole of the morning
the bunch had become a photograph in a report
The bunch of the whole thing
A bunch, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: tie a bunch 意为“扎一束（花）”，1958 年母亲被派去扎一束她抱不动的花。
bunch 意为“束”，指那些花本身而不是绳子，共九枝，由最后走的人拿走。
bunch 指厅里每一束花，每一束都是同样的缎带。
bunch 指前面那一束（女孩捧的那一束），是唯一有人认真扎好的。
bunch 意为“束”，抽象指它所代表的聚会，父亲说 bunch 就是那个上午的全部。
bunch 为抽象用法，指那场聚会本身，是村子里人人都带、却没人质疑的东西。
bunch 意为“束、串”，到 1972 年这束 bunch 成了报告里的一张照片。
bunch 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九枝花和十一年的捆扎。
bunch 意为“一束”，我记得的是前面那一束，1976 年被送出去，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
bunch 为抽象总称，祖母说一束花是唯一会因为被送出去而变好的东西。
